reason: E2 explicitly states that anti-oxidation coatings are required for high-temperature air applications of HfMoNbTaTi, a closely related alloy, supporting the premise that coatings are a viable intervention. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence that a coating prevents oxygen embrittlement without sacrificing mechanical properties in HfNbTaTiZr; E1 only discusses embrittlement mechanisms without mentioning coatings, and E2 makes no mechanical-property comparison for coated vs. uncoated alloys. The key premise of maintained mechanical performance is thus unsupported.
premises: Anti-oxidation coatings can improve high-temperature oxidation resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys
HfNbTaTiZr suffers from oxygen embrittlement at high temperatures
A coating can prevent oxygen embrittlement without degrading mechanical properties
The cited evidence supports the need for anti-oxidation coatings on similar alloys
